title: Plan entitlements and usage credits
description: Server-side plan features and limits with subscription-status fallback and grace, plus an append-only usage-credit ledger with idempotent grants and debits, expiring credits, holds and optimistic concurrency.

notes: Requires a TypeScript build and crypto.randomUUID: Node.js 22+, Bun, Deno, Cloudflare Workers, Next.js route handlers and Hono.
Framework-neutral; there is no HTTP adapter because entitlement checks belong inside your own request handlers.
No runtime packages, environment reads, timers or network activity at install or import time.

configuration: Declare plans with feature flags and numeric limits (Infinity for unlimited) and choose the fallback plan for canceled, unpaid and post-grace past_due accounts.
Load the Account (plan, status, pastDueSince, overrides) from your billing state, for example a Stripe subscription synced by webhook; never from the request.
Count current usage from your own data inside the same transaction that creates the resource, then call canUse.
Implement CreditStore on your database: one row per ledger entry with a unique (account_id, version) so a stale append fails.
Use a stable idempotency key per business event (payment intent id, job id) for grant, debit and reserve.
limitations: Does not talk to a billing provider, create subscriptions or invoices, or sync webhook state.
canUse is only race-free when current usage is counted in the same transaction that creates the resource.
Balances are replayed from the ledger; very long ledgers need periodic snapshots in your store.
The in-memory credit store is for tests and prototypes only.
Pricing, tax, refunds and consuming-application acceptance remain project responsibilities.

behaviors: features and limits follow the plan, with per-account overrides on the account's own plan
past_due keeps the paid plan inside grace, then falls back; canceled and unpaid fall back at once
overrides never upgrade the fallback plan
a retried debit or grant with the same key changes nothing; the same key with a different amount is refused
debits never take the balance below zero
expiring credits are consumed first and forfeited after expiry
holds reserve credits; capture charges part and returns the rest; release and expiry return all; a retried capture cannot charge twice
five concurrent debits against 100 credits charge exactly three; the version check makes the others re-decide
a store that keeps losing the race surfaces a conflict

changes: First release: plan entitlements and the usage-credit ledger.
